name: Higgs (higgsjs/Higgs JavaScript JIT)
baseline: V8 (its baseline compiler; its optimizing Crankshaft compiler is faster than Higgs)
workload: 26 JavaScript benchmarks run on Higgs, a basic-block-versioning JIT for x86-64, versus V8 compilers, as reported in the DLS 2015 paper 'Extending Basic Block Versioning with Typed Object Shapes' (arXiv 1507.02437).
claimed_speedup: Snippet only (paper not opened, arxiv.org is blocked): a WebSearch result summary says Higgs outperforms the V8 baseline compiler on all but one of 26 benchmarks, with speedups of up to 682%, but lags behind V8's Crankshaft, which performs 49% better on average. The Higgs README itself carries no benchmark numbers.
tradeoffs: Research JIT written in D (needs the DMD compiler), x86-64 and POSIX only, needs GNU make and GNU time. Not callable from C++ without embedding a D runtime.
caveats: Weak claim: it beats only V8's baseline (non-optimizing) compiler, and by the same summary loses to Crankshaft on average. The numbers come from a search-result summary of an arXiv paper that could not be opened here, so the paper's exact figures, hardware and V8 version are unverified; the paper itself is peer-reviewed (DLS 2015) and its artifact is this repo. Licence: no LICENSE file in the repo root and no GitHub licence badge, but source-file headers (e.g. source/main.d) state a Modified BSD licence with three clauses (opened). Last commit 2023-06-09 (a build/Python 3 pull request). Re-tier if a copy of the paper is reachable.
found_via: Hacker News: WebSearch restricted to news.ycombinator.com, query 'Show HN JavaScript engine written in C++ JIT faster than V8 benchmark' (HN thread 'LLVM based JavaScript JIT that beats V8 on Asm.js benchmarks' came with an arXiv 1507.02437 result naming Higgs); README, source header and commits page opened on github.com.

name: Copapy
language: Python (tracing compiler) with C runner and stencils
baseline: NumPy 2.3.5 (also a pure-Python case in tests/benchmark.py)
workload: 30,000 iterations of sum((v1 + i) @ v2 for i in range(10)) with vector length v_size varied from 10 to 500; Copapy traces the expression, compiles it once with its copy-and-patch compiler and calls one compiled function per iteration, while the NumPy version vectorises the loop with np.sum((v1 + i) @ v2).
claimed_speedup: README shows a chart (docs/source/media/benchmark_results_001.svg) in which Copapy is faster than NumPy 2.3.5 over v_size 10 to 500; the README text gives no numeric speedup. It attributes the lead to lower call overhead (one Python call per iteration versus three for NumPy) and notes the chart shows no sign that NumPy's SIMD catches up as v_size grows.
tradeoffs: Not a general-purpose JIT: a tracing copy-and-patch compiler for statically typed numeric computation graphs aimed at deterministic realtime use (x86_64, ARM32, AArch64 and RISC-V); generated code makes no syscalls and needs no libc; the C runner builds with GCC (tail-call optimisation required). Hardware I/O is not yet available per the README.
caveats: Baseline is NumPy, not PyPy, V8, LuaJIT or HotSpot; the win is small-vector call overhead, and the README says the Copapy case moves no data between Python and compiled code. Numbers exist only as a chart image, not in text. tests/benchmark.py (opened) builds the NumPy arrays as float32; Python version, GCC flags and NumPy build are not stated. A @cp.jit decorator exists for ordinary Python functions, but the README benchmark does not cover it.
found_via: Hacker News: HN thread 'Show HN: High deterministic real time in Python with copy and patch compiler' (WebSearch restricted to news.ycombinator.com, query 'Show HN copy-and-patch JIT baseline compiler'); README, LICENSE, tests/benchmark.py and commits page opened on github.com.
